thread:
mia: Heads up — hosted-eu p99 jumped from ~180ms to ~1.1s around 06:12 UTC and stayed elevated for ~6m. I’m seeing kernel-selector churn + a KV cache eviction storm coincident with the runtime rollout. Posting snippets below.

ton y: seeing the same in dashboards. queue depth spiked (max q=42) and enqueue latency p95 rose. Could be noisy neighbor or a cold-path regression.

sanjay: can you paste the kernel-selector logs? last rollout tweaked heuristics to prefer int8 kernels for longer seqs.

mia: log snippet: ```
kernel_selector: chosen_kernel=fast_int8 seq_len=1024 est_latency_ms=120 backend=rtx-a2 fallback_threshold_ms=900
kernel_selector: chosen_kernel=fallback_fp16 seq_len=1024 est_latency_ms=940 backend=rtx-a2
kvcache: shard=hotshard-7 evict_rate=3000/s hot_count=48
```

eli: quick profiler summary: ```
hotshard: tenant=acme svc=hosted-eu gpu_ms=8100 cpu_ms=2300 kv_hits=2% kv_evictions=67%
kernel_swap_count=1188 priming_time_ms=4200
```

leah: ops recorded a scale-down at 06:09 then scale-up at 06:13. autoscaler removed some warm instances then later added pods back.

ops-bot: autoscaler: scale_down pool=hosted-eu-gpu-1 at 06:09 triggered by idle-3m; scale_up at 06:13 triggered by queue-depth > 30.

tony: timeline fits: scale-down removed warm kernels / primed state -> initial requests hit cold kernels (fallback) -> kernel-selector oscillates between fast_int8 and fallback_fp16 -> long tail latencies + KV cache thrash as many requests re-populate caches.

sanjay: hypothesis: kernel cost model mis-ranked int8 vs fp16 after rollout telemetry change. selector started choosing int8 for long sequences but kernel priming cost + cache pressure made effective latency worse, causing retries/queueing. recommend pinning kernel-selector to previous policy and disabling the new heuristic immediately on hosted-eu for 30m.

mia: doing a canary revert on hosted-eu-canary now, then will roll back cluster-wide if metrics look good.

leah: opened incident INF-2026-412, added logs + traces + dashboard links. tagging runtime/infra/sre.

mia: canary result: p99 back to ~190ms after pin (within 2 min of revert). rolling full revert to previous selector.

sanjay: follow-ups: (1) add a gate for kernel-selector changes that requires queued-sample pass (2) fix cost-model tuning for long sequences (3) add a safeguard to prevent excessive per-tenant KV evictions during warm-state loss.

eli: also propose a short-term mitigation: limit kernel swaps per-request and add a priming budget so newly-created pods warm kernels before serving long-seq traffic.

mia: agreed. will capture action items in the postmortem and schedule a working session. will close thread after revert completes. :thumbsup:
